See docs/INDIA_STATE_INVESTMENT_INCENTIVES.md.

sample_project_matrix.note: Land rate: AIDC-confirmed, official, dated EOI (EPIP Amingaon; a minimum base auction rate, actual allotment may be higher). This is the one entry in this matrix with a CONFIRMED STACKABLE central+state combination: Assam's own state scheme plus the central North-East-specific UNNATI package on top -- a genuine finding, not an assumption. UNNATI's real-world disbursement reliability is separately flagged as unverified in docs/INDIA_CENTRAL_INVESTMENT_INCENTIVES.md-style research.

Land rate: DDA-confirmed (Mangolpuri Industrial Area e-auction reserve price) -- but from a 2022 auction cycle (DSIIDC's own portal was unreachable in this research pass), so treat as dated. NO state-tier incentive is modeled: Delhi has NO notified, state-style industrial investment-promotion policy with capital/interest/SGST mechanics as of this research -- a Draft Industrial Policy 2025-2035 remains unnotified, and industrial investment there is governed almost entirely by central schemes. This project's extreme land cost (the highest of all states in this matrix, reflecting genuine urban land scarcity) combined with zero state incentive makes it the least favorable entry here on both dimensions.

Land rate: a Collector/circle rate (UT's own minimum stamp-duty valuation floor, Industrial Area Phase III, eff. 01.04.2025), NOT a Housing Board/Estate Office allotment or auction premium -- the actual allotment portal could not be reached, so treat this as the weakest-confidence land figure in this matrix. NO state-tier incentive is modeled: Chandigarh (a UT administered directly by the Centre) has no finalized industrial investment-promotion policy of its own; a draft is in stakeholder consultation. Industrial investment is effectively governed by central MSME schemes only.

Land rate: press-verified against the official J&K Industrial Land Allotment Policy 2021-30 (Zone A, Rs5 lakh/Kanal). A genuinely new investment today cannot access it -- a third distinct 'no incentive in practice' story alongside Delhi/Chandigarh (never existed) and West Bengal (revoked).

Land rate: CONFIRMED, official, primary PDF fully read (Ladakh Industrial Land Allotment Policy 2023, >20 Kanal urban tier) -- the best-sourced land figure of this entire research effort, and the lowest per-acre rate in the whole matrix. NO incentive is modeled: Ladakh's own UT policy (Sustainable Industrial Policy 2022-27) was keyword-searched directly and confirmed to have zero capital-subsidy, interest-subvention, or GST-linked mechanic; a separate central scheme (Rs3,500cr since FY2023-24) exists but its exact rates could not be confirmed, so none is assumed.
